items.title: The Lake of No Heat, Indra's Palace, and Jambudvīpa's Name

items.zh: 即於此側，有無熱大池，其量深廣各五十踰繕那；微細金沙遍布其底，八支德水彌滿其中，形色殊妙，端嚴憙見。從此派流為四大河。一名殑伽，二名信度，三名私多，四名縛芻。
items.en: Beside this, there is the great Lake of No Heat, fifty yojanas in depth and breadth alike; fine golden sand covers its floor, and it is filled with water of the eight excellent qualities, its form and colour wondrous, dignified, and a joy to behold. From here flow four great rivers: the first named Gaṅgā, the second Sindhu, the third Sītā, and the fourth Vakṣu.

items.zh: 復次，於蘇迷盧頂處中，建立帝釋天宮，縱廣十千踰繕那量。所餘之處，是彼諸天村邑聚落。其山四面，對四大洲，四寶所成。謂對贍部洲，琉璃為面；對毘提訶，白銀為面；對瞿陀尼，黃金為面；對拘盧洲，頗胝為面。
items.en: Further, at the very centre of Mount Sumeru's summit stands the palace of Śakra, ten thousand yojanas in extent. The mountain's four faces, corresponding to the four great continents, are made of four precious substances: facing Jambudvīpa, its face is lapis lazuli; facing Pūrvavideha, silver; facing Aparagodānīya, gold; and facing Uttarakuru, crystal.

items.zh: 又贍部洲，循其邊際，有輪王路，真金所成，如四大王天有情膝量，沒住大海。若輪王出世，如彼膝量海水減焉。又無熱池南有一大樹，名為贍部，是故此洲從彼得名。
items.en: Further, along the edge of Jambudvīpa, submerged in the ocean to the depth of a Cāturmahārājika god's knee, lies the road of the wheel-turning king, made of true gold. When a wheel-turning king arises in the world, the sea recedes to that same depth, and the road appears. Further, south of the Lake of No Heat stands a great tree named Jambu — hence this continent takes its name.

items.zh: 次於此北、有設拉末梨大樹叢林，四生種類妙翅諸鳥栖集其中。此四大洲各二中洲以為眷屬。復有一洲，羅剎所住。如是器世間成已，有諸有情從極淨光天眾同分沒，來生此中。餘如前說。此皆由彼感劫初業。此業第一，最勝微妙，欲界所攝；唯於此時此業感果，非於餘時。爾時有情名劫初者。又彼有色從意所生。如是一切，如經廣說。彼於爾時，未有家宅及諸聚落。一切大地面皆平正。
items.en: Next, north of this, there is a forest of great śālmalī trees, where garuḍa birds of all four kinds of birth gather and roost. Each of these four great continents has two intermediate continents as its retinue. There is one further continent, where rākṣasas live. When the receptacle world has formed in this way, beings pass away from the company of the Radiant Light gods and are born here. The rest is as explained before. All this comes from their karma that produces the first age of the eon. This karma is the foremost, most excellent and subtle, and belongs to the desire realm; it bears fruit only at this time and not at any other. The beings of that time are called the first-age beings. They have form, and it is born of mind. All this is as explained at length in the sūtras. At that time there were not yet any houses or villages, and the whole face of the earth was level.

items.title: The Earth's Savory Essence Appears — and Is Then Hoarded

items.zh: 自此以後，由諸有情福業力故，有地味生。如是漸次，地餅、林藤，不種粳稻，自然出現，無糠無𥝖。次有粳稻，有𥝖有糠。次復處處粳稻叢生，於是有情方現攝受。
items.en: From this point on, through the power of beings' meritorious karma, a savory essence of the earth arose. Gradually thereafter, earth-cakes and forest-vines likewise appeared; and rice arose of itself, unsown, without husk or bran. Later, rice appeared with husk and bran. Then rice began growing everywhere in clusters, and it was then that beings first began to hoard it.

items.zh: 次由受用味等資緣，有情之類惡色便起，光明遂滅。其多食者惡色逾增，身極沈重。此諸有情互相輕毀，惡法現行。由此因緣，所有味等漸沒於地。
items.en: Next, through consuming this flavour and similar sustenance, an unpleasant complexion arose among beings, and their inner light was extinguished. Those who ate more developed an even worse complexion, and their bodies grew extremely heavy. These beings then began to disparage and disrespect one another, and unwholesome conduct became active. Through this, the earth's savory essence and the like gradually vanished from the ground.
As explained at length in the sūtras.

items.title: Desire, Houses, Land, and the First King

items.zh: 復從此緣，諸有情類更相顧眄，便起愛染。次由能感男女業故，一分有情男根生起，一分有情女根生起。遞相陵犯，起諸邪行，遂為他人之所訶呰，方造室宅以自隱蔽。
items.en: Then, through this same cause, beings began to gaze upon one another, and craving arose between them. Then, through karma capable of producing male and female, some beings developed male organs, and others female organs. They began to violate one another, giving rise to improper conduct, and, being reproached by others for this, they built houses to conceal themselves.

items.zh: 復由攝受粳稻因故，遂於其地復起攝受。由此緣已，更相爭奪，不與取法從此而生。即由此緣立司契者，彼最初王名大等意。如是便有剎帝利眾、婆羅門眾、吠舍眾、戍陀羅眾出現世間。
items.en: Further, because of hoarding rice, beings then began to appropriate the land itself. Through this, they fell to fighting over it, and the practice of taking what is not given arose from this. It was for this very reason that an arbiter was established, whose first king was named Mahāsammata, "the Great Elect." In this way, the classes of kṣatriya, brāhmaṇa, vaiśya, and śūdra came to appear in the world.
The stages by which this came about are as explained at length in the sūtras.

items.zh: 又彼依止光明既滅，世間便有大黑闇生，日月星宿漸漸而起。
items.en: Further, once the light these beings had depended on was extinguished, the world fell into great darkness, and the sun, moon, and stars gradually arose.

items.title: Sun and Moon: Size, Substance, and Motion

items.zh: 其日輪量五十一踰繕那。當知月輪其量減一。日輪以火頗胝所成，月輪以水頗胝所成。此二輪中，月輪行速及與不定。又彼日輪，恒於二洲俱時作明，復於二洲俱時作闇。謂於一日中，於一日出，於一夜半，於一日沒。
items.en: The sun measures fifty-one yojanas. The moon's measure, it should be understood, is one less. The sun is composed of fire-crystal; the moon is composed of water-crystal. Of these two orbs, the moon's motion is swift and irregular. The sun, moreover, always illuminates two continents at once while simultaneously darkening the other two: within a single day, one continent has its sunrise, one its midnight, and one its sunset.

items.zh: 又一切所有日月星宿，歷蘇迷盧處半而行，與持雙山高下量等。
items.en: Further, all the suns, moons, and stars move around Mount Sumeru at half its height, level with the height of the Yugaṃdhara mountains.

items.zh: 又復日行時有遠近，若遠蘇迷盧，立為寒分；若近蘇迷盧，立為熱分。即由此故，沒有遲速。又此月輪，於上稍欹，便見半月。由彼餘分障其近分，遂令不見。如如漸側，如是如是漸現圓滿；若於黑分如如漸低，如是如是漸現虧減。由大海中有魚鼈等影現月輪，故於其內有黑相現。
items.en: Further, the sun's course varies in distance from Mount Sumeru: when far, this is established as the cold season; when near, the hot season — and this variation is also why sunset comes earlier or later through the year. Further, when the moon tilts slightly, only half of it is seen, its remaining portion obstructing the near portion from view. As it tilts further, it appears fuller and fuller; in its waning half, as it lowers further, its light gradually diminishes. The dark markings seen within the moon are the reflected shadows of great fish and turtles in the ocean.

items.zh: 諸星宿中，其量大者十八拘盧舍量，中者十拘盧舍量，最小者四拘盧舍量。
items.en: Among the stars, the largest measure eighteen krośas, the middling ten krośas, and the smallest four krośas.

blocks.text: The physical world is now formed. Today beings arrive in it, and the treatise tells a story of decline from radiance to labour, property, and government. Buddhist tradition preserves the same story in the *Aggañña Sutta* of the Pāli canon. It is worth reading as social psychology: each stage begins with a small act of craving.

Several passages are missing from Ru-Yi's translation (now supplied in our own translation, marked as ours): 0287b24–c05 (north of Jambudvīpa is a great śālmali forest where the garuḍa birds of all four kinds of birth live; each continent has two lesser continents, and one more is inhabited by rākṣasas; then beings come from the Radiant Light heaven and are born here, with bodies of their own light, feeding on joy); 0287c12 and 0287c21 ("as explained at length in the sūtras"); 0287c28 (all suns, moons, and stars travel at half the height of Sumeru, level with Yugandhara); and 0288a07 (the largest stars measure eighteen krośas, middling ones ten, the smallest four).

subs.head: The Lake of No Heat and Jambudvīpa's name

blocks.text: North of the Himalaya lies the **Lake of No Heat**, source of four great rivers. Mount Sumeru's four faces are each of a different substance; the face towards Jambudvīpa is lapis lazuli, which is why our sky is blue. South of the lake stands a great **jambu** tree, "hence this continent takes its name". Venerable Miào Jìng: "It is named for the tree, and the tree in turn is named for gold", which is why 贍部洲 is glossed "the continent of superior gold". Indra's palace on the summit of Sumeru is also described here.

The first beings, come down from the Radiant Light heaven, shine with their own light and need no food. Then a **savoury essence of the earth** (地味) appears. They taste it, and the story of decline begins: "an unpleasant complexion arose among beings, and their inner light was extinguished". Those who ate more grew heavier and duller; they began to compare and disparage one another; unwholesome conduct arose, and the essence vanished. Earth-cakes and forest vines followed, then rice that grew by itself without husk, then rice with husk; and with each step people began to store food, and the food that had grown freely ceased to grow by itself.
The lesson is about craving, not food: each loss follows directly from grasping and comparison.

"Beings began to gaze upon one another, and craving arose." Venerable Miào Jìng notes that 眄 means looking askance, a sidelong, improper look; Ru-Yi's "gaze" is more neutral than the Chinese. Sexual conduct appeared, then houses to hide it, then the division of land into fields, and then theft, "taking what was not given".

To settle disputes, beings chose one among them as arbiter and agreed to give him a share of their grain. He is called **Mahāsammata** (大等意, "the Great Elect"). Master Cháng Bǎi stresses that the first king was chosen by common consent, not appointed by heaven; Venerable Miào Jìng adds that the arbiter's role means making laws everyone agrees to keep. From the same population, sorted by occupation, came the four classes of society. Master Cháng Bǎi points out that this directly rejects the view that the classes were born from different parts of Brahmā's body: all descended together from the same heaven.

The sun measures fifty-one yojanas and is made of fire-crystal; the moon is one yojana less and made of water-crystal. They travel around Mount Sumeru. The treatise explains day and night, the seasons, and the waxing and waning of the moon by their courses.

None of this is offered as astronomy to be defended. The point is that light, time, and the seasons, like everything else in this account, belong to the shared world that beings' karma brings into being and that each being's mind then experiences.

quiz.q: Mount Sumeru's four faces each correspond to a continent and are made of a different precious substance. What is the face towards our Jambudvīpa made of?
quiz.why: "Facing Jambudvīpa, its face is lapis lazuli; facing Pūrvavideha, silver; facing Aparagodānīya, gold; and facing Uttarakuru, crystal." One passage of Master Cháng Bǎi's lecture swaps gold and crystal, which does not match the text; for examination purposes, follow the text. (The later tradition that our sky looks blue because of this face is not in the treatise.)

quiz.q: According to the treatise, where does the name "Jambudvīpa" come from?
options: from the name of its first king
south of the Lake of No Heat stands a great tree named Jambu, from which this continent takes its name
quiz.why: "South of the Lake of No Heat stands a great tree named Jambu — hence this continent takes its name." Venerable Miào Jìng: "It is named for the tree, and the tree in turn is named for gold" — matching the gloss "Continent of Superior Gold." Elsewhere he links the name to gold in a river, but for examination purposes follow the text: it is named for the tree.

quiz.q: After the earth's savory essence appeared, what does the treatise say appeared next, in order?
options: earth-cakes and forest-vines, and unsown rice without husk or bran; later, rice with husk and bran
quiz.why: "A savory essence of the earth arose. Gradually thereafter, earth-cakes and forest-vines likewise appeared; and rice arose of itself, unsown, without husk or bran. Later, rice appeared with husk and bran. Then rice began growing everywhere in clusters, and it was then that beings first began to hoard it." Master Cháng Bǎi's lecture cites the *Ekottara Āgama*: the earth's essence tasted like sweet grape wine. Venerable Miào Jìng found in a dictionary that "forest-vine" is a sweet vine with honey-like sap.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what happened once beings consumed the earth's essence and similar food?
options: an unpleasant complexion arose and their light was extinguished; those who ate more grew very heavy; they disparaged one another, unwholesome conduct arose, and the essence gradually vanished
quiz.why: "Through consuming this flavour and similar sustenance, an unpleasant complexion arose among beings, and their inner light was extinguished. Those who ate more developed an even worse complexion, and their bodies grew extremely heavy. These beings then began to disparage and disrespect one another, and unwholesome conduct became active. Through this, the earth's savory essence and the like gradually vanished from the ground." Master Cháng Bǎi: the earth's abundance withdraws not as punishment but as a natural consequence of moral decline. Venerable Miào Jìng: with heavy bodies they could no longer fly and lost their powers — the reverse of C.

quiz.q: The treatise says an arbiter was appointed once fighting over land and taking what was not given arose. How do the two teachers explain the first king?
options: named Mahāsammata, "the Great Elect," chosen by common consent — not divinely appointed; Venerable Miào Jìng says the "arbiter" means making laws everyone agrees to keep
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi (in the Ru-Yi reading note): the first king was elected by common consent rather than divinely appointed — the treatise's account of the origin of kingship; his lecture glosses Mahāsammata as "the great assembly rising together, of one mind, setting him up as their head." Venerable Miào Jìng: "I take 契 here to mean legislation — people set out laws, one by one, which everyone must keep." A is exactly what the passage rules out.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the size and substance of the sun and moon?
options: the same size, both of gold
the moon is fifty-one yojanas, the sun one less
the sun is made of water-crystal
the sun is fifty-one yojanas, made of fire-crystal; the moon one less, made of water-crystal
quiz.why: "The sun measures fifty-one yojanas. The moon's measure, it should be understood, is one less. The sun is composed of fire-crystal; the moon is composed of water-crystal." B swaps sun and moon; C swaps fire- and water-crystal. Venerable Miào Jìng: crystal here is like quartz, but finer. The text adds that the moon's motion is "swift and irregular."
